_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Vanuatu covering Melanesian settlement (~3000 BCE, Lapita), Polynesian outlier influence, European contact (Pedro Fernández de Quirós 1606, named 'Tierra Australis del Espíritu Santo'), sandalwood trade/blackbirding, Anglo-French Condominium (1906-1980, 'Pandemonium', dual administration), John Frum cargo cult (Tanna), Nagriamel movement (Jimmy Stevens), independence 1980 (Republic of Vanuatu), kastom culture, kava culture, 2015 Cyclone Pam, 2023 earthquakes.

other_languages: 113 indigenous languages (most linguistically dense per capita)

religion.note: Presbyterian (John G. Paton Scottish missionaries, largest denomination); Anglican (Melanesian Mission, Church of Melanesia); Catholic (Marist missionaries, Francophone islands); Seventh-day Adventist (~12%); Assemblies of God; Church of Christ; kastom (traditional beliefs, strong especially on Tanna, coexist with Christianity); John Frum cargo cult (Tanna island, WWII-era, worship American serviceman figure, February 15 celebrations, still active, predict material wealth through ritual); Prince Philip Movement (Tanna, Yaohnanen village, believed Prince Philip was divine being, continued after his death 2021, transferred to King Charles)

ethnic_groups.name: Ni-Vanuatu (Melanesian)
ethnic_groups.notes: Melanesian; extreme cultural/linguistic diversity (113 languages for 335k people, most linguistically dense per capita in world); kastom (traditional culture, land-diving Pentecost, grade-taking ceremonies, nakamal kava-drinking, sand drawing UNESCO); Big Man system (achieved leadership, pig-killing grade ceremonies, tusked boars as currency/status); matrilineal in some islands, patrilineal others; subsistence economy (garden/fishing, 80% population); nakamal (community meeting house, kava drinking place); land is communal/customary (98.5%, cannot be sold to foreigners, only leased, major political issue); Bislama (creole English, lingua franca, unifies diverse peoples)

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Chinese (~1k, small business); Vietnamese (colonial Francophone legacy); European (~500, Australian/NZ/French); Polynesian outliers (Futuna, Aniwa, West Uvea, Mele, culturally distinct Polynesian pockets in Melanesia); Ni-Vanuatu diaspora growing (NZ seasonal worker scheme, Australia)

independence.from: Anglo-French Condominium (New Hebrides; unique dual colonial administration ended; Espiritu Santo brief rebellion/Coconut War suppressed by PNG troops)

country_profile.notes_unique: Land diving / Naghol (Pentecost Island, original bungee jumping, men jump from 20-30m wooden towers with vines tied to ankles, yam harvest ritual, courage test, centuries-old tradition, inspired modern bungee, April-June season, tourist attraction but authentically dangerous); Anglo-French Condominium / 'Pandemonium' (1906-1980, unique colonial arrangement: British AND French administered simultaneously, two police forces, two courts, two education systems, two hospitals, two currencies, two official languages, absurdly duplicated bureaucracy, ni-Vanuatu subjects of neither, 'Condominium of the New Hebrides', widely mocked as inefficient); most linguistically dense nation (113 indigenous languages for ~335k people, one language per ~3,000 people, extreme isolation of islands/valleys, Bislama creole unifies); John Frum cargo cult (Tanna island, WWII-era, followers await return of 'John' (possibly from 'John from America'), annual February 15 celebration with mock military marches/American flag-raising, believe in spiritual means to obtain Western goods, still active with followers, anthropologically famous); Prince Philip Movement (Tanna, Yaohnanen village, believed Duke of Edinburgh was divine/descended from mountain spirit, exchanged gifts with Philip who acknowledged them, movement continued after Philip's death 2021, some transferred belief to King Charles); kava culture (strongest kava in world, daily nakamal sessions, social/political/spiritual, Vanuatu kava exported globally, 'national drink'); sand drawing (UNESCO Intangible Heritage, elaborate geometric designs drawn in sand/volcanic ash, mnemonic/artistic/ritual function, unique to Vanuatu); Cyclone Pam (March 2015, Category 5, 90% structures damaged, 75 km/h+ winds, $450M damage, existential for small nation); most disaster-prone country (World Risk Index #1 repeatedly, cyclones/earthquakes/volcanoes/tsunamis); active volcanoes (Yasur on Tanna, most accessible active volcano, tourists walk to rim, 'lighthouse of the Pacific'; Ambae eruption 2018 evacuated entire island ~11k); Espiritu Santo (WWII US base, Million Dollar Point underwater refuse, SS President Coolidge wreck diving); no income tax (tax haven, Vanuatu Financial Centre, offshore banking, passport-by-investment programme ~$130k); kastom (traditional governance alongside Western law, National Council of Chiefs/Malvatumauri advisory role)
